h1: An open-source OpenClaw alternative that stays inside your browser
lede: {name} acts for you inside the browser’s fence: its own files, the folders you open, the sites you allow, code in a sandbox. It asks before anything leaves. Nothing to install, and ready for a company’s IT.
facts: Do it, Ask me first, Never
try.ask: A plan for the office move in March: who does what, and by when.
fair.title: OpenClaw, fairly
fair.body: OpenClaw is one of the most popular open-source AI assistants. You run it on your own computer or a server and talk to it from WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Signal and other chat apps. It can run commands, read and write files and browse, and with its skills read and send email, even while you’re away. That reach is its strength, and the risk its own security guide spells out: a message it reads can carry instructions. A flaw rated 8.8 out of 10 was disclosed and fixed in January 2026.
fence.title: Two ways to give an AI hands

fence.otherCaption: An assistant with the run of the computer can do more, and so can a message that tricks it.

Installed on your computer or a server, as one gateway program.
In the tab, typing or speaking.
From your chat apps: WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Signal, Discord, iMessage and more.
Its own files, the folders you open, the sites you allow. Code runs in a sandbox. Your computer only through This computer, in the folder you start it in, each command asked first.
Commands, files and a browser; with its bundled skills, email and a password manager.

better.title: Where OpenClaw does better
better.items: It works while you’re away, and you reach it from the chat apps on your phone.
It runs any program on your machine: if a command can do it, it can.
A large community writes skills for it, shared on ClawHub.
both.title: Coming from OpenClaw
both.cards: {name} reads skills written as SKILL.md, the same format. Those that need no program outside the browser work as they are.
Services you reach by their address connect to {name} too, signed in from the browser; the others go through a gateway.
When a program on your computer is needed
This computer runs it, through a line you paste and can stop at any time, asking first.
catch.items: {name} works while it is open. Your chat apps can’t reach it.
Outside the fence, some jobs need This computer: a line to paste, on a computer.
{name} is free; the AI behind it may not be.
Your work lives in this browser. Clear its data without a backup and it’s gone.
faq.items: Is there an OpenClaw alternative for companies?
{name} is deployed like a web page, from your own address, answering only through your AI gateway and your sign-in. See {enterprise}.
Can a web page or an email trick {name}?
It can try, as with any AI. What it reads can’t open the fence, and sending, deleting and anything outside still ask you first.
Yes, MIT: about 29,000 lines, small enough to read.
end.title: An AI with hands, inside a fence
